bihar_raw_news.title: Goat Rearing Scheme Brings Financial Stability to Gujarat's farmers - ANI News
bihar_raw_news.content: Goat Rearing Scheme Brings Financial Stability to Gujarat’s farmers Updated: 5 hours, 30 min ago A government livestock scheme is helping farmers in Gujarat build sustainable livelihoods. In Jamnagar’s Tamachal village, Hathabhai Chavaliya turned to goat rearing after struggling with employment and financial difficulties. With government support, he purchased 10 goats and one buck - and started a new livelihood for his family. The initiative has brought Hathabhai a regular source of income, greater financial stability and confidence. Under the Animal Husbandry Department’s goat-rearing scheme, beneficiaries receive assistance up to 1.20 lakh rupees for purchasing goats, along with support for fencing, shelter and fodder. Along with financial assistance, the government provides veterinary services to support livestock health and productivity. Such initiatives are encouraging rural families to take up livestock farming, create sustainable sources of income and move towards greater self-reliance. These initiatives reflect the government’s efforts to strengthen rural livelihoods by supporting livestock farmers at every stage. By promoting livestock farming and providing financial as well as veterinary support, the government is helping families build sustainable incomes and become self-reliant. bihar_raw_news.content: September 12, 2026 48 lakh hit as Bihar floods spread across 15 districts Copy Link X WhatsApp Share By Pioneer News Service Source: PTI The flood situation in Bihar deteriorated on Saturday, with the number of affected people increasing to nearly 48 lakh across 15 districts, while several rivers, including the Ganga, were flowing above the danger levels. The Water Resources Department (WRD) cautioned against sudden and rapid riverbank erosion, and directed its officials to maintain close vigil at vulnerable locations. “Due to the rise in water levels of several rivers, approximately 47.92 lakh people in 575 gram panchayats across 87 blocks in 15 districts have been affected by the floods," the Disaster Management Department said in a statement issued on Saturday. The flood-hit districts are Patna, Bhojpur, Saran, Vaishali, Bhagalpur, Begusarai, Buxar, Samastipur, Munger, Katihar, Lakhisarai, Khagaria, Purnia, Madhepura and Araria. The count of flood-affected people was 47.33 lakh on Friday evening. The government also instructed officials to ensure prompt reporting of any erosion incident and to keep adequate resources readily available at vulnerable locations. Incessant rain in Bihar, coupled with downpours in catchment areas of Nepal, has caused several rivers and streams to swell, officials said. The state has recorded 104.1 mm of rainfall in September so far, about 27 per cent above normal, they said. The Disaster Management Department said the Ganga at Sultanganj in Bhagalpur was flowing at 36.48 metres at 6 am on Saturday, 1.98 metres above the danger level, though the water level was receding. The water levels of the Gandak at Dumariaghat, the Kosi at Baltara and Kursela, the Burhi Gandak at Khagaria, the Ganga at Digha, Gandhi Ghat, Hathidah, Bhagalpur, Kahalgaon and Munger, the Punpun at Sripalpur, the Bagmati at Benibad, and the Ghaghra at Darauli and Gangpur Siswan were flowing above the danger marks, the Water Resources Department said. It stated that a sudden reduction in water levels could increase the risk of bank erosion, posing a threat to vulnerable stretches of riverbanks and embankments. The department officials have been directed to immediately inspect any location showing signs of sudden erosion, bank collapse, or rapid movement of the river current towards the bank, and to initiate necessary preventive and protective measures without delay. “A total of 1,245 community kitchens are being operated in various districts for flood-affected people. In addition, 13 relief camps remain functional. In these facilities, arrangements for accommodation, food, medical care and other essential items have been made for 12,260 flood-affected people”, the Disaster Management Department said. So far, approximately 3.50 lakh polythene sheets, 57,100 dry-ration packets and 1,400 food packets have been distributed among flood-hit people. A total of 1,840 boats are being operated to facilitate evacuation and transportation, it said, adding that so far, 11,204 quintals of animal fodder have been distributed. In view of floods and to ensure prompt relief and rescue operations, 27 SDRF teams and 10 NDRF teams have been deployed in various districts. bihar_raw_news.title: RJD announces candidates for six seats ahead of Bihar MLC polls
bihar_raw_news.content: Politics 11 Sep, 2026 RJD announces candidates for six seats ahead of Bihar MLC polls Business To Business, Patna, 11 September 2026: The Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) has intensified preparations for the upcoming elections to eight seats in the Bihar Legislative Council, announcing candidates for six constituencies while discussions over the remaining two are still underway. The elections will be held for four Teachers' Constituency and four Graduates' Constituency seats. The terms of the sitting MLCs are scheduled to expire on November 16, 2026, with the election process expected to be announced in September. Unlike Assembly elections, the Teachers' and Graduates' constituencies have a specialised electorate. While political parties are preparing their candidates, a number of Independent candidates are also expected to enter the contest. According to a list issued by the office of RJD state president Mangnilal Mandal, the party has named Dr Sanjiv Kumar Singh as its candidate for the Patna Teachers' Constituency and Dilip Kumar for the Patna Graduates' Constituency. The party has also fielded Nitesh Kumar from the Kosi Graduates' Constituency, Anil Kumar Jha from the Darbhanga Graduates' Constituency, Prof. Jayram Yadav from the Saran Teachers' Constituency and Dr Rashmi Vinayak Gautam from the Tirhut Graduates' Constituency. The RJD said discussions are continuing over the selection of candidates for the two remaining seats. Their names will be announced after the party finalises the candidates. With the tenure of the sitting MLCs approaching its end, political parties have stepped up preparations across the eight constituencies. The RJD has already outlined its strategy for several key seats, particularly in the Patna Teachers' and Graduates' constituencies. Among the four Teachers' Constituency seats, Prof. Naval Kishore Yadav of the BJP represents Patna, Dr Madan Mohan Jha of the Congress represents Darbhanga, Afaque Ahmad, an Independent, represents Saran, and Sanjay Kumar Singh of the CPI represents Tirhut. In the four Graduates' Constituencies, Neeraj Kumar of the JD(U) represents Patna, Sarvesh Kumar, an Independent, represents Darbhanga, NK Yadav of the BJP represents Kosi, and Banshidhar Brajvasi, an Independent, represents Tirhut, and their tenure will be completed in November this year. The specialised nature of the electorate is expected to make the contests different from conventional Assembly elections. Among the Teachers' Constituencies, Patna has the largest voter base with 16,689 registered voters, followed by Saran with 10,800, Tirhut with 9,204 and Darbhanga with 8,967 voters. The Graduates' Constituencies have substantially larger electorates. Tirhut has approximately 1.35 lakh voters, followed by Kosi with around 1.34 lakh, Darbhanga with nearly 1.27 lakh and Patna with about 88,000 voters. Alongside established political parties, Independent candidates are also preparing to campaign among teachers and graduates in their respective constituencies. bihar_raw_news.title: High-level review meeting regarding preparations for 'Seva Sankalp Abhiyan' concludes ...
bihar_raw_news.content: High-level review meeting regarding preparations for 'Seva Sankalp Abhiyan' concludes under chairmanship of Chief Secretary of Bihar ANI 11 Sep 2026, 22:29 GMT+10 Patna (Bihar) [India], September 11 (ANI): A high-level review meeting was held under the chairmanship of Bihar Chief Secretary Pratyaya Amrit to discuss the comprehensive preparations and successful implementation of the 'Seva Sankalp Abhiyan' (Service Pledge Campaign), scheduled to take place from September 17 to October 17. According to a press release, Principal Secretaries and Secretaries from various state departments attended the meeting in person, while District Magistrates from all districts joined via video conferencing. During the review, the Chief Secretary assessed the department-wise status of all 13 key components of the campaign and directed officials to complete preparations in a time-bound manner. The release noted that the campaign will commence on the evening of September 17 with the 'Aashirwad ka Diya' (Lamp of Blessing) program, involving the collective lighting of lamps in every household across the state and at a minimum of 10 prominent or symbolic public locations in each district. To facilitate this, lamps will be distributed to beneficiaries through Jeevika, urban local bodies, and the Public Distribution System. Additionally, between September 17 and October 7, painting and speech competitions based on the theme 'Viksit Bharat Sankalp' (Developed India Pledge) will be organised in all government and private schools under the 'Seva Chitra' initiative, alongside Parent-Teacher Meetings (PTMs). To raise public awareness, 18-20 theatre troupes will be formed under the 'Seva Smaran' (Service Remembrance) initiative; these troupes will perform street plays in schools, colleges, and panchayats, with special performances scheduled for October 2, the release said. Furthermore, a three-day event titled 'Aangan ka Milan' (Gathering in the Courtyard) will be held at all Anganwadi centres from September 25 to October 7. This event will feature the honouring of Anganwadi and ASHA workers, interactions with beneficiary mothers, and recreational activities for children, alongside the dissemination of information regarding nutrition and health schemes, the release added. To highlight the positive changes brought about in people's lives by government schemes, district and state-level digital data banks will be created by compiling authentic reels and short videos under the 'Kahani Badlav Ki' (Story of Change) component. Additionally, 'Seva Jyoti Yatra' will feature foot marches, as well as bicycle and motorcycle rallies across the state and districts; volunteers from 'Mera Yuva Bharat' will participate in these events, culminating in a collective pledge for 'Viksit Bharat 2047' (Developed India 2047). As the nationwide 'Vadnagar to Varanasi (Jal, Jan, aur Seva Sankalp Yatra)' passes through Bihar, arrangements will be made for grand receptions, security, accommodation, and interactions with local beneficiaries at designated stopover points, the release noted. To foster public participation, 25 activities, including the cleaning of ponds and Chhath ghats, tree plantation, and sanitation drives, will be conducted under the 'Seva Mera Yogdan' (Service: My Contribution) initiative, ensuring visible, on-ground transformation at a minimum of two locations in every assembly constituency. national_raw_news.content: The 18th BRICS Summit will begin at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi tomorrow, with the national capital putting its finishing touches in place for the grand event. The two day Summit will bring together eleven major emerging and developing economies, including Brazil, China, Egypt, Ethiopia, Indonesia, India, Iran, Russia, Saudi Arabia, South Africa, and the UAE. The theme of India’s Chairship 2026 is “Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability.” World leaders including Russian President Vladimir Putin, Chinese President Xi Jinping, President of South Africa Cyril Ramaphosa, Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi, Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto, Iran President Masoud Pezeshkian, Crown Prince of Abu Dhabi Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed al Nahyan and Prime Minister of Ethiopia Abiy Ahmed Ali will participate in the Summit. Brazil will be represented by Foreign Affairs Minister Mauro Vieira. Saudi Arabia’s Minister of Foreign Affairs, Prince Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud will also participate in the Summit. Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim, and Vietnamese Prime Minister Le Minh Hung are the other Heads of State who will attend the Summit. United Nations Secretary General António Guterres, Director-General of WHO, Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, and President of New Development Bank, Dilma Rousseff are among the Heads of International Organisations who will participate in the event. Prime Minister Narendra Modi is likely to hold bilateral talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin today. The President of Russia and Foreign Minister of Brazil arrived in the national capital last night to participate in the Summit. The President of South Africa is set to arrive this morning. Presidents of Iran, Indonesia, Egypt, Philippines, and Burundi, Crown Prince of Abu Dhabi, and Prime Ministers of Malaysia and Ethiopia, are scheduled to arrive later today. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will have a series of bilateral meetings on the sidelines of the Summit. Akashvani correspondent reports that the grouping was formalised during the BRIC Foreign Ministers’ Meeting, held on the margins of the United Nations General Assembly in New York in September 2006. The First BRIC Summit was held in Yekaterinburg, Russia, on 16th June 2009. BRIC expanded into BRICS with the inclusion of South Africa following the BRIC Foreign Ministers’ Meeting held in New York in September 2010. South Africa participated first time in the Third BRICS Summit, held in Sanya, China, in April 2011. BRICS further expanded in January 2024, when Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, Saudi Arabia and the UAE became full members of the grouping. India assumed the BRICS Chairship on 1st January this year. This marks India’s fourth Chairship of BRICS. India had earlier chaired BRICS in 2012, 2016 and 2021.

national_raw_news.title: 6 hours ago | National 140 India beat Bangladesh by 40 runs in first semi-final of Women’s Asia Cup 2026
national_raw_news.content: In Cricket, India produced a brilliant all-round performance to thrash Bangladesh by 40 runs in the first semi-final of the Women’s Asia Cup 2026 in Dubai last night. India’s victory secured their place in the Women’s Asia Cup 2026 final, with the second semi-final between Sri Lanka and Pakistan determining their opponents. Chasing a target of 150 runs, Bangladesh struggled to build momentum as India’s bowlers kept the pressure on and made 109 for the loss of seven wickets in the stipulated twenty overs. Shorna Akter, unbeaten 22, was the top scorer for Bangladesh. For India, Deepti Sharma scalped three wickets, Nandani Sharma took two wickets, while Shree Charani and Prema Rawat claimed a wicket each. Earlier, Bangladesh won the toss and opted to field. Put in to bat, India posted 149/6 in 20 overs, with opener Shafali Verma anchoring the innings with a fluent 64 off 40 balls. She was declared Player of the Match. The victory sets up a mouth-watering final for Team India. In the second semi-final today, Pakistan will face Sri Lanka in Dubai. The match will start at 8 PM Indian Standard Time. The winner of that contest will meet India in the final on Sunday. With strong all-round contributions and a dominant bowling display, India have underlined their credentials as favourites to lift the Women’s Asia Cup 2026 title.
